articles.body: 화면 끄라는 AI, 화면 켜서 눈 고치는 VR — GrowWise와 AmblyoPunch가 만난 지점 Hacktoberfest 'Touch Grass' 챌... 지난 가을, 나는 해커톤 시즌을 맞아 Hacktoberfest ‘Touch Grass’ 챌린지에 참여하기로 했다. 평소엔 오픈소스 기여를 위해 PR을 던지는 게 일상이었지만, 이번에는 ‘화면을 끄라는 AI’와 ‘화면을 켜서 눈을 고치는 VR’이라는 모순된 문구가 머릿속을 맴돌았다. 내 눈은 이미 오래전부터 약시(amblyopia) 증상으로 흐릿했고, 의사는 “스크린 타임을 줄이라”고만 반복했다. 그런데 VR 헤드셋을 쓰고 훈련용 콘텐츠를 돌리면 오히려 시력이 개선될 수 있다는 이야기를 들었다. GrowWise와 AmblyoPunch라는 두 프로젝트 이름이 동시에 등장했고, 나는 그 둘이 어떻게 만나는지 직접 확인해보고 싶었다. 1. 프로젝트 탐색과 첫 인상 GitHub에서 growwise/vr-amblyopia 와 amblyopunch/training-core 리포지토리를 클론했다. 둘 다 MIT 라이선스로 공개되어 있었고, README에는 “실시간 시선 추적 데이터 수집”과 “적응형 렌더링 파이프라인”이라는 키워드만 적혀 있었다. 문서화는 최소한이었지만, 이슈 트래커에는 “Unity 2022.3 + OpenXR 1.5에서 동작 확인”이라는 코멘트가 있었다. 나는 곧바로 로컬 머신에 Unity Hub를 열고, OpenXR 플러그인을 추가한 뒤 샘플 씬을 빌드해보았다.

articles.title: The first screen of my Android AI app asks for an API key. That's where most people give up
articles.excerpt: My app has passed 200 downloads, and the most useful feedback I've had so far wasn't about a feature. It was one person on a forum telling me, twice, that he couldn't get past step one. Quick context:…
articles.body: My app has passed 200 downloads, and the most useful feedback I've had so far wasn't about a feature. It was one person on a forum telling me, twice, that he couldn't get past step one. Quick context: Kryzz AI is an MIT-licensed Android app (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose) for chat, voice and agent tasks. It doesn't run models on the phone. You bring your own OpenRouter key and the models are hosted by whichever provider you pick. Chats, memory, files and keys stay on the device, and there's no analytics or telemetry. Bring-your-own-key has a cost, and the user pays it first I picked BYOK on purpose. No server of mine sits between you and the model, I never see your prompts, and I don't need to charge a subscription to cover API bills.

articles.title: I built a token killer for AI agents. Here's what it didn't kill.
articles.excerpt: 🔪 I built a token killer for AI agents. Here's what it didn't kill. When an agent reads a web page, it pays for the whole page. On GitHub's page for psf/requests, that's 123,176 tokens. Only 519 of t…
articles.body: 🔪 I built a token killer for AI agents. Here's what it didn't kill. When an agent reads a web page, it pays for the whole page. On GitHub's page for psf/requests, that's 123,176 tokens. Only 519 of them are the README. 🤯 The rest is navigation menus, sign-in banners, file lists and scripts. leantext is an open-source tool (Apache-2.0) that turns what an agent reads into lean Markdown. It strips page chrome, keeps the content, checks the result against the source, and reports tokens before and after. It handles HTML pages, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, and PDFs, including scanned ones via OCR. I benchmarked it on well-known pages, then checked line by line what it threw away. Both results are below, including where it still loses data.

articles.title: Making AI Memory Capture More Reliable Across Multiple Agents
articles.excerpt: I've been building a local AI memory system that allows different agents to share persistent context through a Markdown repository. The system worked, but I noticed a recurring problem: agents sometim…
articles.body: I've been building a local AI memory system that allows different agents to share persistent context through a Markdown repository. The system worked, but I noticed a recurring problem: agents sometimes forgot to save important information , even when their instructions explicitly required it. This made memory capture inconsistent, especially when switching between different AI tools. Separating Capture from Processing I redesigned the architecture to separate conversation capture from memory processing. The updated workflow has three stages: Capture: Tool-specific integrations collect supported conversation events and place them in a shared queue. Process: A separate workflow evaluates captured information and identifies what deserves long-term storage.

articles.title: Stop Inventing Custom API Errors: A Guide to RFC 7807 Problem Details
articles.excerpt: RFC 7807 Problem Details is an official technical specification that defines a standard JSON format for describing errors returned by HTTP web APIs. Instead of having every software engineer create th…
articles.body: RFC 7807 Problem Details is an official technical specification that defines a standard JSON format for describing errors returned by HTTP web APIs. Instead of having every software engineer create their own custom fields like message , err_code , or reason , this standard establishes predictable key names such as type , title , status , detail , and instance . This gives both computer programs and human developers a uniform way to understand exactly what went wrong during an API request. The Everyday Analogy: Car Diagnostic Reports Imagine taking your car to a mechanic when the check engine light comes on. Option A: The mechanic hands you a piece of paper that simply says: "Car is broken.

articles.title: Zammad's two flaws were chained in seconds by an automated agent, and the second one is about service accounts
articles.excerpt: Zammad's two flaws were chained in seconds by an automated agent, and the second one is about service accounts A helpdesk platform is not usually treated as critical infrastructure. It holds the conve…
articles.body: Zammad's two flaws were chained in seconds by an automated agent, and the second one is about service accounts A helpdesk platform is not usually treated as critical infrastructure. It holds the conversations a company has with its customers, the email addresses of everyone who ever opened a ticket, and, in most deployments, a trusted connection to the directory that authenticates employees. In late September 2026, two zero-day flaws in Zammad were used together to take one such platform from an unauthenticated request to root on the host, and the victim was an organisation whose entire job is handling vulnerability reports. The two flaws CVE-2026-102489 is a session hijack vulnerability in Zammad 6.3.0 through 6.5.4 that leads to remote code execution as the zammad service user.

articles.title: Record breaker! Astronomers spot powerful cosmic explosion that lasted 27 days
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have spotted a remarkable gamma-ray burst that's a real Incredible Hulk compared to other cosmic explosions of the same type.
articles.body: Astronomers have spotted a remarkable gamma-ray burst (GRB) that's a real Incredible Hulk compared to other cosmic explosions of the same type. What makes this GRB so special is the fact that the central engine powering it remained active for around 27 days, flaring in X-rays following the initial blast. That's 20 days longer than the longest previous GRB on record. This record-breaking burst — which is designated GRB 220706A and was spotted on July 6, 2022 — is even more exciting because scientists don't know what the central engine powering it actually is. "In a nutshell, GRB 220706A is an extremely late X-ray flare.
